solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Balance not found on TV?

parts.note: something not found on is off, as a light that is not on
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A puzzled viewer wonders why a balance is never shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset something is to counterbalance it, as gains offset losses.

clue.text: Serious criminal's fine advancing hand-out

indicators.note: advancing means the letter for fine moves forward within the word for the prisoner

parts.note: a lifer is a criminal serving a life sentence, so one guilty of a serious crime
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A dangerous convict is paid a penalty and handed a handout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancing' moves the F of LIFER one place forward, before the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a printed leaflet handed out to passers-by.

clue.text: Hand in wrapper from stolen produce

indicators.note: in means the word for hand sits inside the outer letters picked from stolen
the wrapper of a word is its first and last letters, which enclose the rest

parts.note: a paw is an informal word for a hand

explanation.surface: A hand reaches into the packaging of some stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapper from stolen' gives S and N, the first and last letters; 'in' puts PAW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and frogs spawn when they lay eggs, so to spawn is to produce offspring.

clue.text: An inspiring passage?

parts.note: inspiring is taken literally as breathing in, and the passage is the tube air travels down to the lungs

explanation.surface: A stirring paragraph in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the airway carrying inhaled air from the throat to the lungs.

clue.text: Finishing touch for pub toilet — porcelain looking radiant

indicators.note: the finishing touch of a word is its last letter

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A pub's lavatory is given a final flourish of gleaming china.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooming describes someone flushed with health and glowing, as a blooming bride.

clue.text: Comb is integral to this hairdo

definitions.meaning: honeycomb is built inside the home of a bee colony
a tall rounded bouffant hairstyle of the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: Bees build honeycomb inside their hive, and the tall domed 1960s hairstyle is named after that shape.

clue.text: Tinder-mad idiot regularly head over heels, leaving for New York

indicators.note: head over heels means upside down, so in a down entry the picked letters are read in the opposite direction
regularly means taking every other letter, here the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A fool obsessed with a dating app falls in love and heads off to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, N, E, M, D, D, O from 'Tinder-mad idiot'; 'head over heels' turns them round. 'for New York' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaving is something left over, as is a remnant or scrap.

clue.text: Note street artist going round shops

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: going round means the abbreviations for street and artist are turned to face the other way

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

explanation.surface: A busker turns to make a note while passing the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; the surface's street artist is a busker, not a pavement painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Small convenience stores are called by this name, a compact version of a supermarket.

clue.text: It's consumed by small group welcomed by Mother Teresa, perhaps

definitions.text: It's consumed by small group welcomed by Mother Teresa, perhaps

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the nun, so the rest sits inside her

parts.note: Mother Teresa was a nun, a famous example

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed by, so the word it goes inside the trio

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food is shared among a few people taken in by a famous missionary nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother Teresa is a famous nun, hence 'perhaps'. Read whole, the clue describes the food her order handed out to the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is the sustenance eaten by the hungry, the nourishment the missionary handed out.

clue.text: Minister's housing six clubs for golf in lock-up

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, here the six clubs replace golf

parts.note: a lock-up is a garage that can be locked
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
VI is six in Roman numerals
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A government minister keeps a set of golf clubs in his garage.
explanation.walkthrough: VIC replaces the first G of GARAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Mark periodically using dye on goatee

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone tints their goatee with dye, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes D, E, N, O, T, E from 'dye on goatee'; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to indicate or signify, as a symbol marks something.

clue.text: Short BRIO Channel broadcast showing supplementary track

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
short means cut down, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: A toy train company's brief television channel shows a side railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the O of BRIO, a wooden toy train brand; 'broadcast' rearranges BRI and CHANNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch line is a secondary railway route feeding a main line.

clue.text: Letters for Massachusetts and Illinois?

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois

explanation.surface: A question about the postal codes for two US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Post consists of letters delivered by the postal service.

clue.text: Key adult behind step up

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
A is the film certificate for adult
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: An important grown-up falls behind and must take a step up.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to intensify or increase, as a conflict grows.

clue.text: Picking rising stars with no head for business can start to grate

indicators.note: rising means going up, so in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top
with no means a letter is removed

parts.note: celebs are celebrities, stars

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Choosing up-and-coming stars with no business sense can start to grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head for business' drops B from CELEBS to leave CELES; 'rising' turns it into SELEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking means choosing, the same as selecting.

clue.text: Missing beginning and end of class, pacify a teacher in school

indicators.note: missing means letters are lacking from the words that follow

parts.note: to calm is to pacify
a master is a schoolteacher

indicators.note: the beginning and end of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A teacher misses the start and end of class while trying to calm a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning and end of class' gives C and S; 'Missing' removes them from CALM A MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is Latin for nourishing mother, used for the school or university one attended.

clue.text: Passionate Dickens character swapping sides

indicators.note: swapping means exchanging, so the letter at one edge of the name trades places with the other
sides here are the two ends of the character's name, its first and last letters

parts.note: Little Dorrit is a Dickens heroine

explanation.surface: A Dickens character switches allegiance in a passionate affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping sides' exchanges D and T, the first and last letters of DORRIT, Dickens's heroine of Little Dorrit.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid means intensely ardent, as a torrid love affair.

clue.text: Former student's article following endless slander

indicators.note: following means the article comes after the trimmed word
endless means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: calumny is slander
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A former pupil's piece follows endless defamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips C and Y from CALUMNY to leave ALUMN.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female graduate of a school or college.

clue.text: Cultivated a lot of tropical fruit

indicators.note: cultivated means worked or tilled, so the letters are worked into a new order
a lot of means most of, here the word minus one letter

explanation.surface: Lots of tropical fruit has been cultivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the L of TROPICAL; 'Cultivated' rearranges TROPICA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Service still no good

parts.note: even so means still, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, a service is still no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Upcoming spread full of Private Eye's witty writing

indicators.note: full of means one word contains the other
upcoming means coming up, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
a private eye is a private investigator, a PI

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Private Eye is full of witty writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' turns MARGE into EGRAM. Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, which steers away from the detective.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short clever saying or poem.

clue.text: Implement carried by seamen for centuries

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held within these words

explanation.surface: A tool has been carried by sailors for hundreds of years.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a rule is to put it into effect, to make it apply.

clue.text: Dodge as icicle falls, smashing, taking only seconds

indicators.note: taking only seconds means picking the second letter of each word

explanation.surface: An icicle drops and shatters in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or swindle, a con.

clue.text: Maybe Amazon Fire not as reliable at first for translation

indicators.note: at first means the first letter only
for translation means rendered into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amazon's Fire tablet is not as dependable at translating.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fire is Amazon's tablet, but Amazon here is the river's jungle. 'at first' gives R; 'for translation' rearranges FIRE NOT AS into AINFOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon basin holds the world's largest tropical jungle.

clue.text: Provoke arguments on podcast

indicators.note: on podcast means heard spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: rows are noisy arguments

explanation.surface: Picking fights on a podcast to get a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or incite.

clue.text: Skin issue dermatologist keeps in check

indicators.note: keeps in check means holds within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A dermatologist controls a skin problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather made from the napped underside of animal hide.

clue.text: Tribute possibly holding nothing back, I see, covering all of life

indicators.note: back means the letter for nothing moves further back in the word

parts.note: an obit, short for obituary, is a tribute to someone who has died
O is zero, nothing
C sounds like see

explanation.surface: A tribute that holds nothing back covers someone's whole life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding nothing back' moves the O of OBIT one place back, giving BIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Biotic describes everything relating to living organisms.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by grief at intervals, chose different approach?

indicators.note: at intervals means every other letter, here the second and fourth

parts.note: routed means utterly defeated, overwhelmed

explanation.surface: Someone swamped by grief finds a new way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes R and E from 'grief'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send by a different path.

clue.text: Plant a reddish-pink flower — time to replace borders of narcissi

indicators.note: to replace means one letter goes in where others were

parts.note: geranium is a flower and also the name of a reddish-pink colour

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gardener swaps a pink flower for narcissi at the edge of the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of narcissi' gives N and I; T replaces that NI in GERANIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageratum is a garden plant with fluffy blue flower heads.

clue.text: Ring setter on phone line with terms of lucrative contract

indicators.note: on phone means heard spoken, so the letter is given by its sound

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: terms means ends, so the last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A crossword setter calls about a line in the terms of a lucrative deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is I, which said on the phone sounds like EYE; 'terms of lucrative contract' gives E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord.
